scope: Generic vector search and explicit interrupt scheduling. Real campaign binding and full-game verification are recorded separately.

oracle.method: Independent finite-tree enumeration of vector Max-N decisions, exact chance expectation, and an explicit fixed-opponent policy expectation.
oracle.claims: Finite-budget correctness and approximation checks on these fixtures; no claim of a global optimum, Nash equilibrium, or full-game playing strength.
oracle.action_order_result: Identical per-action counts and value vectors for each paired budget, seed and fixture.
additional_fixtures: Stochastic outcomes route to Allies and Comintern reaction owners; exact expected chosen-action vector [4, 3.5, 4], 4096 simulations, seed 73, component tolerance 0.4.
Fixed donation policy v1 is sampled in both search and actual opponent choices; exact target action value [8, 2, 0], 4096 simulations, seed 4, target value tolerance 0.3.
Depth-limited values are explicitly evaluator approximations; terminal roots return the exact three-component terminal vector.

Changing maximum depth invalidates shallow cached rollout values and bounds: a 512-simulation depth 1 search prefers the immediate 1 payoff; both reused-object and fresh 128-simulation depth 8 searches prefer the delayed 10 payoff under a deliberately pessimistic intermediate evaluator.

verified_contracts: Each decision maximizes its entitled player's component without sign flips.
Chance has no policy owner; every simulation independently seeds a search clone and samples explicit chance events.
Actual execution state and its RNG are unchanged by search.
Action edges retain complete-state successors; explicit chance nodes retain multiple sampled outcome states.
Cache identities include complete planning state, rules, evaluator version, opponent mode, target, opponent-policy version and maximum rollout depth.
Observed root reuse requires exact complete-state identity.
Optimistic first-play urgency, PUCT components and optional selection traces remain inspectable; children are not forced to receive one visit each.
Root noise is local to the current root opportunity, including reused internal nodes and cycles.
Interrupt offers and passes are explicit entitled-player decisions; the engine retains mandatory declaration priority.
Interrupt pass state survives clone and checkpoint restore and participates in observation/planning identity.
Raw unhandled interrupt opportunities are rejected rather than silently skipped.
